surfaces.part: window glass with night sky and moon (flat pane)
left and right wooden shutters (vertical faces)

answer.evidence: The object is a window drawn face-on, with a stone frame, a night-sky pane at rows 4-26 and two vertical shutters. Its width profile is a constant 30 px from rows 4-26 and 32 px at the sill. Nothing in rows 2-26 is a horizontal surface: the lintel at rows 2-3 is a 1-2 row strip and the shutters are flat vertical faces. The only ledge-like part is the sill at rows 27-29, a 3-row light band with a darker 2-row face at rows 30-31. It is a minor detail, not the main body. The main body is a flat, wall-mounted front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 19 visible tones per tile, against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. Its near-flat coverage is 11%, close to the stall's 13%. 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted, with dark blue-brown beside the frame and shutters and no uniform black sticker line. By eye, the frame and shutters step through about 5 tones with a lit edge and grain. The night sky has a gradient, scattered stars and a crescent moon, so it is not one flat fill. It is slightly simpler than the best references (the well and the stall). Even so, a careful artist would accept it next to them without it looking thinner or flatter.
